summary: Whole-chapter independent Chinese-source reading completed: all 67 owned units, 93 temporal/hint items and 17 people explicitly checked. Not approved. Found borrowed relative-death attestations, appraisal dates incorrectly treated as living activity (including Cao Can after death), a Ruyi death-month Western-year boundary, Fei/Cao calendar and primary-witness conflicts, mixed conventional/converted hints, lost inherited context, installation-versus-marriage overprecision, omitted Gaozu posthumous reception, and an actual misplaced sixth-year source heading. Explicit age five is retained without inventing a birth; generic service/age thresholds and capping were not turned into personal ages. Valid historical dates dependent on the restored source sequence are qualified, not silently inferred. Research holds remain; no source/extraction/queue edits or paid APIs were used, and no repair is approved.

itemChecks.event: Hui (p001) and Zhang (p013): claimed beginning of their spousal union.
itemChecks.reason: The converted year 192 BC is correct for the establishment on year-four month-ten renyin (Gregorian 7 November). However, 立皇后 dates installation as empress, not explicitly formation of the marriage. Retain the dated status claim; do not present this as an explicit exact union start without evidence.

evidence.quote: 四年冬十月壬寅，立皇后張氏。

itemChecks.event: The clan princess (p009) marries the chanyu (p010).
itemChecks.reason: 嫁 supplies this woman's own marriage, in the third-year narrative after the spring mobilization. Hui year three conventionally labels 192 BC; this is an honestly coarse event year, not a verified Gregorian wedding day. Neither spouse's birth or age follows.

evidence.quote: 以宗室女為公主，嫁匈奴單于。

itemChecks.event: Hui (p001) is reported aged five when Gaozu becomes King of Han.
itemChecks.reason: The numeral five belongs to Hui, not Gaozu. Shiji 22 and the calendar table identify Gaozu's first Han year as 206 BC. Preserve it as the source's traditional reported age, not five completed modern birthdays. No exact birth was inferred; an inclusive calculation of circa 210 BC is not an omitted explicit birth.

evidence.quote: 帝年五歲，高祖初為漢王。

itemChecks.event: Hui (p001) accedes as emperor.
itemChecks.reason: Month five inherits Gaozu year twelve from s0004, not Hui year twelve. Bingyin is day 17 after the gengxu month start: 23 June 195 BC Julian = 20 June 195 BC proleptic Gregorian. The stored year is correct; the Chinese day is retained.

evidence.quote: 五月丙寅，太子即皇帝位

itemChecks.event: Hui (p001) is established as crown prince.
itemChecks.reason: The second year continues Gaozu's kingship chronology from s0002, conventionally 205 BC (206 minus one elapsed year). Shiji 22 independently places establishment of the heir in that year. This is not Hui year two, 193 BC; no Gregorian day is claimed.

itemChecks.event: Gaozu (p002) first holds the title King of Han.
itemChecks.reason: 初為漢王 directly dates Gaozu's own acquisition of royal status. Shiji 22 puts it in Han year one, conventionally 206 BC; it must not be confused with his later imperial accession in year five. No day precision or continuous dynasty activity is asserted.

itemChecks.event: Lu (p003) is honored as empress dowager at Hui's accession.
itemChecks.reason: The empress identified in s0001 becomes dowager in her own right in s0005. Year twelve is Gaozu's; month-five bingyin maps to Gregorian 20 June 195 BC. The son's accession is context, while her honor is explicitly also stated.

evidence.quote: 五月丙寅，太子即皇帝位，尊皇后曰皇太后。

itemChecks.event: Yao (p011) is established as King of Donghai.
itemChecks.reason: 夏五月 inherits Hui year three, not Gaozu year three. The appointment is Yao's own status event, conventionally 192 BC; the reconstructed month lies within that Gregorian year. Chinese summer/month-five wording is preserved.

evidence.quote: 夏五月，立閩越君搖為東海王。

itemChecks.event: Princess Yuan (p006) receives the honor queen dowager from Fei.
itemChecks.reason: 尊公主為太后 explicitly dates the princess's honor during Hui year-two winter month ten. The month spans Gregorian 17 November to 16 December 194 BC. Thus stored 194 BC is a converted event year, not the conventional year-two label 193 BC; this honor is not biological maternity.

evidence.quote: 二年冬十月，齊悼惠王來朝，獻城陽郡以益魯元公主邑，尊公主為太后。

itemChecks.reason: Year-four month-ten renyin fits the reconstructed month, day 13: 10 November 192 BC Julian = 7 November proleptic Gregorian. The explicit installation event and Western year are supported. It does not independently establish a 191 BC event or her age.

evidence.quote: 四年冬十月壬寅，立皇后張氏。

itemChecks.event: Guan Ying (p016) holds the office grand marshal while commanding the forces.
itemChecks.reason: 太尉灌嬰將 identifies his own office and command in Hui year-seven winter month ten. The reconstructed month is Gregorian 21 November-20 December 189 BC, not conventional label 188 BC. This proves office holding then, not appointment on that date or a full term.

evidence.quote: 七年冬十月，發車騎、材官詣滎陽，太尉灌嬰將。

itemChecks.reason: The source explicitly states Gaozu's death before Hui's accession. Gaozu year twelve is 206-(12-1)=195 BC; the reconstructed fourth month lies wholly in 195 BC. No finer day or death age has been invented.

evidence.quote: 十二年四月，高祖 崩。

Retain the source month and represent uncertainty across 195-194 BC, unless independent evidence establishes a day.

evidence.quote: 元年冬十二月，趙隱王如意薨。

itemChecks.event: Liu Fei (p005) dies, recorded as year-six month-ten xinchou.
itemChecks.reason: The year-six tenth month would fall in 190 BC, but begins wushen and has 30 days: xinchou is 53 days after wushen and cannot occur in it. Shiji 22 instead records year-six seventh-month death, in 189 BC. Do not certify the point 190 BC, silently replace the month, or discard the conflicting witnesses.

evidence.quote: 六年冬十月辛丑，齊王肥薨。

itemChecks.event: Cao Can (p014) dies in Hui year-five eighth month.

Shiji 22 reads yichou, which fits, but that is a different primary witness. Preserve both readings and mark the finer chronology unresolved pending independent resolution.

Relation buried-at is not living activity. Shiji 22 has xinsi instead; this check supports the retained Hanshu witness, not a harmonized universal day.
